assessment.nobel_worthiness: A consequential and unusually influential body of evidence on technology, trade exposure, local labour markets, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson provide a coherent core for the empirical mechanisms and distributional consequences; Katz is also foundational to the broader literature.
assessment.maturity: The central findings have shaped labour economics and policy debate for many years and have generated extensive follow-on research.
uncertainties: The discovery combines several linked literatures, making a sharply bounded award citation difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and made place-based inequality central to economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are the indispensable core, with Friedman a major collaborator on the foundational mobility work.
assessment.maturity: The research program is mature, widely replicated in design and highly influential across labour, public, and urban economics.
uncertainties: Its broad empirical reach raises questions about whether the contribution is sufficiently singular for one prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM supplied a durable toolkit for credible empirical work with persistence, fixed effects, and endogenous regressors.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are central to the original estimator, while Blundell's contribution to the system-GMM development is fundamental.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established, broadly used, and their limitations are now well understood.
uncertainties: Routine application and weak-instrument problems have sometimes exceeded the reliability of the method in practice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony gave labour-market institutions and wage setting a more realistic conceptual and empirical basis.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest intellectual anchor for the unified modern monopsony framework; the other named scholars made important but more distinct contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become central to research on wages, concentration, and employment policy and is supported by accumulating evidence.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping spans theory and later empirical work whose appropriate joint attribution is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence experiments made discrimination measurable in real labour-market decisions and changed empirical research and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are the central pair for the field-defining modern audit study; Charles is an important contributor to the wider literature.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively adopted across countries and markets, with a substantial accumulated evidence base.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify differential treatment at specified margins but do not alone establish all mechanisms behind aggregate disparities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life shocks, health, and skill formation substantially altered how economists understand the origins of human-capital inequality.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond anchor influential quasi-experimental evidence, while Cunha is central to the dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: The evidence and theory have had enduring influence in health, education, labour, and public economics.
uncertainties: The empirical and theoretical strands are complementary but not a single tightly delimited discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural models of labour supply and household responses supplied a powerful framework for analysing taxes, incentives, and life-cycle choices.
assessment.attribution: Blundell, Meghir, and MaCurdy each made central contributions to the structural labour-supply tradition represented by the citation.
assessment.maturity: The program has been influential for decades and remains a major component of applied policy evaluation.
uncertainties: Results can be sensitive to modelling restrictions, and attribution overlaps with broader advances in structural econometrics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on teacher effectiveness, school accountability, and educational production has strongly shaped education-policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Woessmann represent especially influential empirical strands, while Hoxby and Hanushek are also major contributors to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: The literature is longstanding, policy relevant, and informed by increasingly credible empirical designs.
uncertainties: The listed work covers several distinct questions and identification strategies rather than one unified discovery.
